formationLabel: Lithuanian parish organized in 1912 · St. Anthony church built in 1913 · merged with St. Stanislaus into St. Francis of Assisi Parish in 1982 · lineage continued into Saint John Paul II Parish in 2013
currentUse: St. Anthony Parish ended through merger in 1982. Official successor history states that St. Francis of Assisi used St. Stanislaus Church, not the former St. Anthony building, and that the 2013 successor Saint John Paul II Parish uses Visitation Church. A field survey reports that the St. Anthony building later served a Church of God in Christ congregation and was subsequently vacant and offered for sale, but gives no observation date or exact address; present ownership, use, and physical condition therefore remain unknown.
summary: St. Anthony was Kewanee's Lithuanian Roman Catholic parish, organized in 1912 with its church built in 1913. The current Saint John Paul II Parish history confirms the Lithuanian identity and resolves the inherited 1982 claim: St. Anthony and the Polish St. Stanislaus parish merged that year to create St. Francis of Assisi Parish, which worshiped at St. Stanislaus Church. In 2013 St. Francis and St. Mary merged into Saint John Paul II Parish, which uses Visitation Church. These are two typed institutional lineage steps, not survival of St. Anthony at its original building. The former St. Anthony church's exact address has not been established in the accepted canon; an undated field survey describes later non-Catholic reuse followed by vacancy and a sale offering, so its current condition remains unresolved. No dedicated cemetery or complete records-custody chain has been verified.

historicalNarrative.text: St. Anthony was a distinct Lithuanian Roman Catholic parish in Kewanee, not the Cicero, Chicago, or other same-name St. Anthony institutions. Wolkovich dates the parish's formation to 1912 and the church to 1913–1914. The current successor parish independently identifies St. Anthony Church as built in 1913 to serve Lithuanians. The dossier therefore separates 1912 parish organization from the 1913 building milestone.

sources.locator: Wolkovich, Lithuanian Religious Life in America, vol. 3, pp. 107–108
Official Saint John Paul II Parish history: St. Anthony Church, 1913, serving Lithuanians

historicalNarrative.text: The official history resolves the previously thin 1982 terminal reading. It says Kewanee's four ethnic Catholic churches were reorganized into two parishes in 1982: St. Stanislaus and St. Anthony became St. Francis of Assisi Parish. This was an institutional merger, not merely a property sale or the end of Lithuanian-language ministry. The new parish continued worship at St. Stanislaus Church, so the former St. Anthony building did not become the successor's Catholic worship site.

sources.locator: Official parish history, 1982 merger paragraph: St. Stanislaus and St. Anthony formed St. Francis and used St. Stanislaus Church

historicalNarrative.text: A second institutional step occurred in 2013. St. Francis of Assisi and St. Mary merged to form Saint John Paul II Parish, which the official history says uses Visitation Church. The dossier models both mergers rather than collapsing St. Anthony directly into the current institution, and it keeps the successor churches distinct from St. Anthony's own building.

sources.locator: Official parish history, 2013 merger paragraph: St. Francis and St. Mary formed Saint John Paul II Parish using Visitation Church

historicalNarrative.text: The former St. Anthony church's later life is less certain than the institutional lineage. A reviewed field survey says the church later served a Church of God in Christ congregation and was subsequently vacant and offered for sale. The source does not give an observation date or exact street address, so the dossier does not elevate that account into a present-tense building label. It records the attributed sequence while leaving ownership, current use, structural condition, and interior condition unknown.

sources.locator: Kewanee field survey, St. Anthony church section: later reuse, vacancy, and sale observation; exact date absent

historicalNarrative.text: No accepted source establishes a dedicated St. Anthony cemetery, a parcel-complete church address, a final Mass date, the disposition of parish records, or the present fate of the church. The official successor history proves current institutional continuity at Saint John Paul II and Visitation Church, but it does not prove that all St. Anthony records are held there or that the former building survives today. Those questions remain explicit gaps.

conflictsWithArchiveRecord: The inherited 'merged 1982' status is confirmed and now typed as the formation of St. Francis of Assisi from St. Anthony and St. Stanislaus. The official history also proves the later 2013 step into Saint John Paul II. The field-survey building account is undated and cannot support a present-tense standing, vacant, or sale status.
gaps: Founding and merger decrees, exact St. Anthony church address and parcel, construction/dedication details beyond 1913, final Mass date, deed and ownership chain, date and duration of Church of God in Christ use, sale outcome, present building and interior condition, complete sacramental-record custody, and any cemetery remain unverified.
